scenario: AITA for expecting family time? | This morning I woke up and saw my husband watching video game streams, his typical pastime. Later he said the streamers he was watching were having cash giveaways that required participation to be entered. He continued to watch while he covertly built the kids' bikes in the garage as I had asked, then left to run a last-minute grocery errand for dinner, then came home and went upstairs to watch more streaming. After wrapping gifts, I did dishes and put dinner in the oven, and asked him to turn it off to spend time with me with/without kids. He said no. That the stream was only for today and it is not okay for me to expect him to stop doing what he finds enjoyable just because I want him to do something I find enjoyable. But if I was okay letting him spend $100 on app purchases for this game (same one he's watching) that he'd shut it off no problem. But last year he spent a little over $2,000 on in-app purchases for this game, and after a lengthy discussion, said he wouldn't buy anymore. So I'm not a huge fan of okaying any more money for it. It's almost 6pm and says he doesn't know when it will end, but that there are 2 more streamers left. I feel like the evening is almost over and I am so disappointed and feel saddened that he would rather watch games than spend time with me. Am I an asshole for being upset and having unrealistic expectations?

But last year he spent a little over $2,000 on in-app purchases for this game, and after a lengthy discussion, said he wouldn't buy anymore. So I'm not a huge fan of okaying any more money for it. It's almost 6pm and says he doesn't know when it will end, but that there are 2 more streamers left. I feel like the evening is almost over and I am so disappointed and feel saddened that he would rather watch games than spend time with me. Am I an asshole for being upset and having unrealistic expectations?

Healthy relationships require both people to actively choose each其他 over hobbies or distractions. You’re NTA. 💡

First, I need to recall the AITA framework. AITA stands for "Am I the Asshole?" and it's a Reddit community where people post scenarios to get judgment on whether their actions were reasonable. - The husband is doing some tasks (building bikes) but then continues streaming when asked to stop for family time.

Now, is the user the asshole for expecting family time? 

In relationships, mutual respect and time together are important. Expecting quality time, especially in the evening after a day of work and chores, is reasonable. The husband is doing some tasks but then choosing to continue streaming instead of engaging with the family. 

The fact that he's willing to stop only if she pays for more in-app purchases is problematic. It's like he's using the in-app purchases as leverage, but the user is right to be hesitant given the previous $2000 spent. 

Also, the cash giveaway might be a justification, but if it's only for today, he could still take a break for family time. Streaming can be paused, and he can come back to it later. 

The user isn't asking him to stop all streaming; just to have some family time. It's not unreasonable to expect that after a day of work and chores, they spend time together. 

The husband's argument that "it's not okay for me to expect him to stop doing what he finds enjoyable just because I want him to do something I find enjoyable" is a bit off. It's not about one activity being more enjoyable than the other; it's about shared time. Family time is a shared activity, and both partners should contribute to it. 

Also, the $2000 spent last year on in-app purchases is a red flag. It shows a pattern of excessive spending on the game, which they had a discussion about. Now he's asking for $100 more, but the user is right to be against it.

Also, the husband's behavior of "covertly" building bikes while watching streams might indicate he's not fully present, but he's still doing the task. However, when asked to stop streaming for family time, he refuses. 

The key is that family time is a shared responsibility. It's not "my activity vs. your activity"; it's about being together. 

Yes, the user is NTA. So answer is 0.
